To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BNLC graph languages are closed under union, intersection, complement, and reversal, but are not closed under the other graph theoretic operations, such as the Boolean operations of set difference, set product, and set sum, or graph operations like disjoint sum and graph complement.

the family of BNLC languages is closed under the following operations: intersection, union, difference (i.e., set complementation), product, concatenation, Kleene star (i.e., Kleene closure), and reversal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
closure properties of the BNLC language family.
closure properties of this family of graph languages with respect to graph theoretic operations.
the investigation of closure properties of the class of BNLC graph languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the closure properties of BNLC languages are exactly the same as those of the languages generated by the family of NLC languages, i.e., the closure properties are the same as the closure properties of the context-free string languages.
the family of BNLC graph languages is not closed under any of the graph theoretic closure properties investigated here.
the family of BNLC languages is a graph theoretic closure class.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have investigated the graph-theoretical closure properties of the class of BNLC languages.
we investigate graph theoretic closure properties (under union, intersection, concatenation, and Kleene star) for the family of BNLC languages.

we have investigated the closure properties of the BNLC language family with respect to graph operations, such as disjoint union, disjoint product, Cartesian product, disjoint sum, and graph homomorphism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BNLC grammars are a natural generalization of the well-known graph grammars which generate languages of trees, i.e., of the tree languages.

the family of BNLC languages is a proper subfamily of the family of NLC languages and that it is not closed under union, intersection, complement and concatenation, but is closed under Kleene star and under homomorphisms.

the family of BNLC graph languages is closed under a number of important graph-theoretic operations: disjoint union, union, intersection, and Cartesian product, as well as the operation of graph complement.
